Hi Anna — thanks for the follow-ups and the timeline. Please find attached the completed SIG answers PDF and a short technical addendum. Key points (summary):

- Prompt & response logs: For the Redwood Hosted API our default conversational logs are retained for 14 days and then deleted; we retain non-identifying metadata (aggregate metrics) for 13 months for observability and billing. Dedicated and Private deployments can have customized retention per contract; default Dedicated retention mirrors Hosted unless otherwise contracted. We do not, by default, archive customer prompt/response logs beyond the configured retention window.

- KV / prefix caches: The runtime uses in-memory KV caches for hot prefixes. These are ephemeral and not persisted to durable object storage under normal operations. On Dedicated nodes we may write compacted checkpoint files only during controlled graceful shutdowns for faster warmup; those checkpoints are short-lived and are deleted within 48 hours by default. We do not use KV cache contents for analytics or model training.

- Model training: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response data to train or finetune any publicly distributed models by default. Customers can opt in to analytics or aggregated-model programs via explicit contractual agreements; opt-outs are recorded in our contract system and apply immediately upon signature of the exclusion. For Private/on-prem deployments, customer-managed infrastructure controls training access.

- Deletion & evidence: Deletion requests are executed via our control plane and produce immutable audit entries (request id and timestamp). For Hosted customers, compliance exports (audit log snippets and deletion confirmations) are available via the Console and as periodic S3 exports upon request.

Attachments included: HealthEdge_SIG_answers_20270804.pdf (completed SIG spreadsheet), redwood-data-handling-playbook-2027.pdf (technical addendum). We also uploaded a small evidence bundle to a shared Drive folder and linked the HubSpot ticket for tracking.
